compareCandidate.label: Element vs. compound
compareCandidate.description: An element is a pure substance of only one kind of atom — gold is all gold atoms. A compound is a pure substance of different elements bonded together — water is hydrogen + oxygen. Elements are the raw ingredients; compounds are the cooked dishes.

processes: Making up everything as raw ingredients
Defining each pure substance by its atom type
plainLanguageExplanation: An element is a pure substance made of only one kind of atom. Gold is an element: every single atom in a gold ring is a gold atom. Oxygen is an element: every atom is an oxygen atom. Carbon, iron, aluminum, helium — all elements. Each element is a unique type of atom, and each is defined by its proton count: any atom with 6 protons is carbon, any atom with 79 is gold, and there is no overlap. Scientists know of about 90 elements that occur naturally on Earth, and a few more that only exist in labs. Here is the amazing part: everything in the universe is built from these ~90 kinds of atoms, arranged and combined in endless ways. The elements are the alphabet of nature — just a few dozen letters, but they write everything: the air, the ocean, your body, the stars. When elements combine by bonding, they make compounds and molecules. But the elements themselves — the pure ingredients — cannot be broken down into anything simpler by chemical means.

whyItMatters: Elements are the pure ingredients of the universe. Everything you can touch, taste, breathe, and see is built from combinations of about 90 elements. Understanding what an element is — and that each is a unique kind of atom — is the foundation for the periodic table, compounds, and all of chemistry.
didYouKnow: You are mostly four elements: oxygen, carbon, hydrogen, and nitrogen make up about 96% of your body's mass.
compareReason: The element-versus-compound split (raw ingredient versus cooked dish) is the most important classification in chemistry — comparing them makes both unmistakable.
